subproblem.title: Approximate tangent planes almost everywhere imply countable rectifiability (Simon Ch. 3, 1.6 ⇐, corrected constant; parent V13)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P Borel with Hⁿ(M) < ∞ (Hⁿ = μHE[n]) and Q : ℝ^P → linear subspaces such that x ↦ (orthogonal projection onto Q(x)) is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x (Q x) holds for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M. Then M is countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable n M).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent V13 (Simon Ch. 3, Theorem 1.6 ⇐ with ε := 2^{−1}16^{−n} instead of the printed 16^{−n}). The type is also that of the unaccepted DAG node cbr_rectifiable_of_approx_tangent, whose pieces cbrr_rectifiable_dim_zero, cbrr_tangent_cone_density_zero, cbrr_uniform_density_on_large_set, cbrr_projection_net, cbrr_cone_claim, cbrr_lipschitz_cover_of_cone_condition, cbrr_rectifiable_of_uniform_density are accepted. μ := Hⁿ⌞M, p_V := orthogonal projection onto V.
1. If Hⁿ(M) = 0 (countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero), n = 0 (M finite, constant maps), n > P (Hⁿ = 0 on ℝ^P) or n = P (identity map) we are done. Let 1 ≤ n < P, ℓ := P − n, π_x := Q(x)^⊥, X_α(π, x) := {y : dist(y − x, π) < α|y − x|}.
2. At x with tangent space Q(x), testing the blow-up convergence against continuous approximations of 1_{B_1} and of the closed cone {dist(y, π_x) ≤ |y|/2} ∩ B̄_1 (which meets Q(x) only at 0) gives μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) → 1 and μ(X_{1/2}(π_x, x) ∩ B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) → 0.
3. Fix ε' > 0 and ε := 2^{−1}16^{−n}. Lusin (applied to a Borel version of x ↦ p_{Q(x)}) and Egorov (applied to the Borel infima and suprema of these ratios over rational radii) give a compact E ⊆ M with μ(M ∖ E) < ε', on which x ↦ p_{Q(x)} is continuous, and δ > 0 with μ(B_ρ(x)) ≥ (1 − ε)ω_nρⁿ and μ(X_{1/2}(π_x, x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ εω_nρⁿ for x ∈ E, ρ < δ.
4. Choose ℓ-planes π_1, …, π_N with every ℓ-plane within 1/16 of some π_j (compactness of rank-ℓ projections), and E_j := {x ∈ E : ‖p_{π_j} − p_{π_x}‖ < 1/16}. Claim: X_{1/4}(π_j, x) ∩ E_j ∩ B_{δ/2}(x) = ∅ for x ∈ E_j. Otherwise for y in it, σ := |y − x|, we get B_{σ/8}(y) ⊆ X_{1/2}(π_x, x) ∩ B_{2σ}(x), so (1 − ε)ω_n(σ/8)ⁿ ≤ μ(B_{σ/8}(y)) ≤ εω_n(2σ)ⁿ, i.e. 1 − ε ≤ 16ⁿε = 1/2, a contradiction.
5. Hence on D := E_j ∩ B_{δ/4}(x₀), |p_{π_j^⊥}(y − x)| ≥ |y − x|/4, so D is the graph of a 4-Lipschitz map over π_j^⊥; its McShane extension (LipschitzOnWith.extend_real) yields a Lipschitz F : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P with D ⊆ F(ℝⁿ). Finitely many balls cover the compact E, so μ(M ∖ ⋃F_k(ℝⁿ)) < ε'.
6. Taking ε' = 1/m for all m, countably many Lipschitz images cover M up to an Hⁿ-null set: M is countably n-rectifiable. ∎
Note: Lusin (SimonGMT) is outside the import closure; accepted cbrr_uniform_density_on_large_set supplies step 3.
proof_key_steps: Densities at tangent points.
Lusin–Egorov and the cone claim with ε = 2^{−1}16^{−n}.
Lipschitz graphs cover M up to null sets.

(T1) Measures μ_j with sup_j μ_j(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U have a subsequence μ_{φ(j)} and a Borel μ (null off U, finite on compacts of U) with ∫f dμ_{φ(j)} → ∫f dμ for continuous compactly supported f with tsupport f ⊆ U, limsup_j μ_{φ(j)}(K) ≤ μ(K) for compact K ⊆ U and μ(G) ≤ liminf_j μ_{φ(j)}(G) for open G ⊆ U. (T2) If X_j ⇀ X in 𝒟_k(U) with admissible representations (μ_j, ξ_j), (μ_X, ξ_X), μ is finite on compacts of U with limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K), f is continuous and μ{f = t} = 0, then ∫_{f<t}ξ_j(ω)dμ_j → ∫_{f<t}ξ_X(ω)dμ_X for ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U). (MM) If μ_j(G ∩ {a<f<b}) < ∞ and Z_j(t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ_j(G ∩ {t−h<f<t}) for t ∈ (a, b), there is a measurable g with liminf_j Z_j(t) ≤ g(t) for a.e. t ∈ (a, b) and ∫⁻_{(a,b)}g ≤ L·liminf_j μ_j(G ∩ {a<f<b}). The vector Riesz theorem gives a Radon μ₀ on U and a Borel field ν with ‖ν‖ ≤ 1 and L(g) = ∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ₀; push μ₀ forward to ℝ^P and put ξ(x)(α) := ⟨c(α), ν(x)⟩ (c the coordinate isometry), so |ξ(α)| ≤ |α| and T(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ.
2. (REP), μ(W) = M_W(T): ≤ since ξ(ω) ≤ 1_{tsupport ω} for admissible ω; ≥ by the positive-envelope identity sup{L(g) : ‖g‖ ≤ f} = ∫f dμ₀, inner regularity and mollification of almost optimal g.
3. (REP), null sets. Let C ⊆ W ⊂⊂ U be compact with Hⁿ(C) = 0. For each coordinate projection p_α, p_α(C) is Lⁿ-null, and m := (p_α)_*(b⟨dx^α, ξ⟩μ⌞W) (b ∈ C_c^∞(W)) satisfies |∫div g dm| = |∂T(b p_α^#γ) − T(db ∧ p_α^#γ)| ≤ ‖b‖_∞M_W(∂T) + ‖db‖_∞M_W(T) for |g| ≤ 1 (dγ = div g dy). Mollifying m and using Gagliardo–Nirenberg (n ≥ 2) or the fundamental theorem of calculus (n = 1) gives |m|(G) ≤ C·Lⁿ(G)^{1/n} for open G, so |m| ≪ Lⁿ. Hence admissible ω satisfy T(ω) = ∫_{W∖C}ξ(ω)dμ ≤ μ(W∖C), so μ(C) = 0; inner regularity extends this to every Hⁿ-null E.
4. (T1): exhaust U by compacts K_m; on each K_m extract weakly convergent subsequences (compact metrizable), diagonalize, represent the limit functional on C_c(U) by Riesz–Markov–Kakutani and push forward; Urysohn functions give limsup_j μ_{φ(j)}(K) ≤ μ(K) and μ(G) ≤ liminf_j μ_{φ(j)}(G).
5. (T2): for ε > 0 choose smooth χ_ε = 1 on tsupport ω ∩ {f ≤ t−ε}, compactly supported in U ∖ (tsupport ω ∩ {f ≥ t}). Then |∫_{f<t}ξ_j(ω)dμ_j − X_j(χ_εω)| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞μ_j(C ∩ {t−ε ≤ f ≤ t}), C := tsupport ω, and similarly for X; weak convergence and the limsup bound give limsup_j |a_j − a| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞(μ(C ∩ {t−ε ≤ f ≤ t}) + μ_X(C ∩ {t−ε < f < t})) → μ(C ∩ {f = t}) = 0 as ε ↓ 0.
6. (MM): F_j(t) := μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < min(t, b)}) is nondecreasing with μ_j(G ∩ {t−h<f<t}) ≤ F_j(t) − F_j(t−h), so Z_j(t) ≤ L·F_j'(t) a.e.; g := L·liminf_j F_j' is measurable, and Fatou's lemma with ∫_a^b F_j' ≤ F_j(b) − F_j(a) gives ∫⁻g ≤ L·liminf_j μ_j(G ∩ {a<f<b}).

On a ball B_r(x) with IMRep R_x of X|_{B_r(x)}, (MR) gives μ_X(G) = R_x.measure(G) for open G ⊆ B_r(x), hence μ_X = R_x.measure on B_{r/2}(x) (π-system of open sets), and (RU) on B_{r/2}(x) gives ξ_X = orient_x μ_X-a.e. there. Source: parent V6–V15 together with T5 and V4(iii) (B. White's tangent-plane argument, Comment. Math. Helv. 64 (1989) 207–220, replacing Simon's Rectifiability Theorem 6.8.1; integrality is read off from slices as in parent V14). Version 2 of this proof makes the three required repairs: (1) Step 8 is parent V11(a)–(e) with its localized construction: R is fixed, Ω := p⁻¹(B_{3R}), the level t is selected with the compact annulus A'' ⊆ Ω̄, only M_Ω(∂Z_k) → 0 is proved and used, the projected currents Y_k live on B_{2R} with M_{B_{2R}}(∂Y_k) ≤ M_Ω(∂Z_k); no global mass of ∂(Γ_k⌞{g < t}) is claimed (it need not tend to 0: for blow-ups of a circle the restriction to a tangent strip has two boundary points); (2) Step 8 contains the measurable hull E_k of the projected carrier, the proof that the projected densities u_k vanish off E_k, the mollifier/BV estimate and the volume comparison giving α_i ≥ 1; (3) the sharp density comparison and the normalization of Hⁿ used in Steps 3–4 are proved in Step 0(d)–(f): the isodiametric normalization μHE[n] ≤ (ω_n/2ⁿ)μH[n] and the Vitali covering with the finite-tail argument of Simon 1.3.5, which removes the enlargement factor 5ⁿ, so Θ^{*n}(Hⁿ⌞M, a) ≤ 1 for Hⁿ-a.e. a ∈ M.
Tools. (SL) = sibling slicing, (RU) = sibling restrict_unique, (REP), (T1), (T2), (MM) = the first two conjuncts of sibling foundations, (RECT) = sibling rectifiable; hypotheses of this statement: (MR), (IMC), (VO), SLIM_{P,d}, LD_{P,d}. Reuse note (not a proof step): the general facts established in Step 0(b), Step 0(d), Step 1, Step 2, Step 3, Steps 6–7, Step 10 and Step 11 are exactly the statements of the comparator-accepted declarations cbr_ci_const_vector_massOn, cbr_ci_euclideanHausdorff_le_isodiametric, cbr_ci_dilation_calculus, cbr_ci_dilation_slice_property, cbr_ci_density_representation, cbr_ci_constant_cycle_planes, cbr_ci_plane_multiplicity_nat and cbr_ci_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_ae_tangent, whose hypotheses (SL), (RU), (MR), (RECT) are character-for-character the frozen types of slicing, restrict_unique, (MR) and rectifiable; a decomposition of this node may reuse them with their identical frozen types. The arguments are nevertheless given in full below.
Notation. n := d + 1, so 1 ≤ n < P. Hⁿ := μHE[n]; Lⁿ := volume on ℝⁿ = Euclid n, and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume); ω_k := unitBallVolume k = Lᵏ(B_1); B_r(x), B̄_r(x) open and closed balls, B_r := B_r(0). |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; for an m-vector ζ (MultiVector P m), |ζ|* := sup{ζ(β) : |β| ≤ 1} (dual norm, attained since the unit ball of |·| is compact) and ‖ζ‖ is its operator norm; ‖ω‖_∞ := sup_x|ω(x)|. An admissible representation of X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) is a pair (μ, ξ) with μ a Borel measure finite on compact sets, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ-a.e. x and all α, and X(ω) = ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) for every test form ω. ISP is the integer slice property of the statement. Currents are added as X + Y := X − (0 − Y).
Step 0 (Preliminaries).
(a) Coefficient norms. (O) For every orthonormal basis f = (f_1, …, f_P) of ℝ^P and every k-covector α, Σ_{j : Fin k → Fin P}α(f_{j(1)}, …, f_{j(k)})² = k!|α|². Proof: write f_i = Σ_l O_{li}e_l with O orthogonal and expand α(f_{j(1)}, …, f_{j(k)}) = Σ_{l}O_{l_1j(1)}⋯O_{l_kj(k)}α(e_{l_1}, …, e_{l_k}); summing the squares over j and using Σ_iO_{li}O_{l'i} = δ_{ll'} gives Σ_{l : Fin k → Fin P}α(e_l)²; non-injective l contribute 0 and each increasing multi-index I contributes k! equal terms α(e_I)² (alternation). Consequences: (O1) if v = (v_1, …, v_k) is orthonormal then |α(v)| ≤ |α| (extend v to an orthonormal basis; the k! permutations of (1, …, k) already contribute k!α(v)²); (O2) β_v(u) := det(⟨u_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} is a k-covector with β_v(v) = 1 and |β_v| = 1 (in a basis extending v its only non-zero values are ±1 on the permutations of (v_1, …, v_k)); (O3) if v = (v_1, …, v_n) is orthonormal in ℝ^P and p(x) := (⟨x, v_1⟩, …, ⟨x, v_n⟩) ∈ ℝⁿ, then the pulled-back covector p^#γ := γ∘(p × ⋯ × p) of an l-covector γ on ℝⁿ satisfies |p^#γ| = |γ| (in an orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P extending v, p(f_i) = e_i for i ≤ n and p(f_i) = 0 for i > n, so the sums in (O) for p^#γ and γ coincide); (F1) ‖α‖_op ≤ Pᵏ|α| (expand unit vectors u_l = Σ_iu_l^ie_i with |u_l^i| ≤ 1; each |α(e_J)| ≤ |α|), hence |ζ|* ≤ Pᵏ‖ζ‖ and |ζ(α)| ≤ |ζ|*|α| for k-vectors ζ; |ζ|* ≤ 1 iff |ζ(α)| ≤ |α| for all α.
(b) Mass of a constant-vector current (accepted cbr_ci_const_vector_massOn). Let ν' be a Borel measure on ℝ^P finite on compact sets, ζ' an m-vector and s ≥ 0 with |ζ'(α)| ≤ s|α| for all α and ζ'(β₀) = s for some |β₀| ≤ 1, and Ξ ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) with Ξ(ω) = ∫ζ'(ω(x))dν'(x). Then M_W(Ξ) = s·ν'(W) for every open W. Proof: for ω admissible for M_W (tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1), Ξ(ω) ≤ ∫_W s|ω|dν' ≤ sν'(W). Conversely take φ_j ∈ C_c^∞(W; [0, 1]) increasing to 1_W (smooth cut-offs equal to 1 on an exhaustion of W by compact sets); φ_jβ₀ is admissible and Ξ(φ_jβ₀) = s∫φ_jdν' → sν'(W) by monotone convergence.
(c) Measures and test functions. If O ⊆ ℝᵏ is open and σ₁, σ₂ are finite Borel measures on ℝᵏ with σ_i(ℝᵏ ∖ O) = 0 and ∫b dσ₁ = ∫b dσ₂ for every b ∈ C_c^∞(O), then σ₁ = σ₂: for open G ⊆ O take b_j ∈ C_c^∞(G; [0, 1]) increasing to 1_G, so σ₁(G) = σ₂(G) by monotone convergence; for an arbitrary open G ⊆ ℝᵏ, σ_i(G) = σ_i(G ∩ O), so σ₁ and σ₂ agree on all open subsets of ℝᵏ, which form a π-system generating the Borel σ-algebra, and σ₁(ℝᵏ) = σ₂(ℝᵏ) < ∞ (Measure.ext_of_generate_finite). Likewise two Borel measures on ℝ^P that are finite on bounded sets and agree on open sets are equal (open sets form a generating π-system and the balls B_m exhaust ℝ^P with finite measure).
(d) Normalization of Hⁿ (accepted cbr_ci_euclideanHausdorff_le_isodiametric, frozen type ∀ (P n : ℕ), (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)) ≤ (unitBallVolume n / 2 ^ n) • (μH[(n : ℝ)] : Measure (Euclid P)); Simon Ch. 1, 2.9–2.10; also SimonGMT simon_theorem_2_10, outside the contract's import closure). Claim: Hⁿ(S) ≤ (ω_n/2ⁿ)μH[n](S) for every S ⊆ ℝ^P, where μH[n](S) = sup_{δ>0}inf{Σ_jdiam(C_j)ⁿ : S ⊆ ⋃_jC_j, diam C_j ≤ δ} is Mathlib's unnormalized Hausdorff measure. Proof: by definition μHE[n] = c_n•μH[n] on every metric space, where c_n := addHaarScalarFactor(Lⁿ, μH[n]) satisfies Lⁿ = c_n•μH[n] on ℝⁿ (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Source: Simon Ch. 6 §5 (5.1, 5.3, Lemma 5.4 and the proof (1)–(38)) in its stated range: degree n := m + 1 ≥ 1, codimension ℓ := P − n ≥ 1; Simon 6.1 for (Isor). Uses (REP) and (MM) of sibling foundations, (SL) = sibling slicing, (RU) = sibling restrict_unique. 1. Tools (Simon 2.17–2.29). For X with compact support and M(X) + M(∂X) < ∞ and Lipschitz F, F_#X := lim (F∗φ_σ)_#X exists (homotopy estimate), ∂F_#X = F_#∂X, M(F_#X) ≤ Lip(F)^kM(X), spt F_#X ⊆ F(spt X), and F_#X depends only on F|spt X. With ∂([[0,1]] × X) = {1}×X − {0}×X − [[0,1]]×∂X and h(t, x) := F(x) + t(G(x) − F(x)): G_#X − F_#X = ∂h_#([[0,1]]×X) + h_#([[0,1]]×∂X) and M(h_#([[0,1]]×X)) ≤ sup_{spt X}|G − F|(Lip F + Lip G)^kM(X).
2. Integrality (Simon 3.3–3.9). The carrier of an IM X is, up to an Hᵏ-null set, a disjoint union of bi-Lipschitz images G_i(A_i) of compact A_i ⊆ ℝᵏ (Rademacher; pieces on which G_i approximates an injective linear map). The area formula and approximate tangent planes on such pieces show that F_#X (F Lipschitz, or locally Lipschitz off a closed set with finite tangential Jacobian integral) is the integral current Φ_F with an integer multiplicity, oriented by the image tangent planes, hence IM; likewise [[0,1]] × X.
3. Faces. For u ∈ L¹((0,1)ⁿ) with divergence variation V: ∫|u − β| ≤ c_nV for every median β, M(∂(u[[(0,1)ⁿ]])) ≤ c_n(V + ∫|u|) (mollified Poincaré and trace inequalities), and if u is integer-valued there is an integer median β with |β| ≤ 2∫|u|, equal to u if V = 0.
4. Retraction (Simon 5.4). For a ∈ B_{1/4}(q), q the cube centre, the dual skeleton L*(a) = a + L_{ℓ−1} has distance ≥ 1/4 from the n-skeleton L_n (needs ℓ ≥ 1), and iterated radial projections from the face points a_F give ψ : ℝ^P ∖ L*(a) → L_n, ℤ^P-equivariant, = id on L_n, |ψ − id| ≤ √P, with pointwise Lipschitz constant ≤ c₁/dist(·, L*(a)) (induction on ℓ; printed 3/4 corrected to 1/4); so Lip ψ ≤ c₂/ρ on {dist(·, L*(a)) ≥ ρ}.
5. Unit scale (Simon 5.1). If T = 0 take Q = R = S = 0. Choose a by the 5r-covering lemma so that μ_T(L*(a; ρ)) ≤ Nβρ^{n+1}M(T) and μ_{∂T}(L*(a; ρ)) ≤ Nβρ^{n+1}M(∂T) for ρ ≤ 1/4. With f := dist(·, L*(a)), (SL), (MM) and Chebyshev give radii ρ*_ν ∈ (2^{−ν−3}, 2^{−ν−2}) with slice mass ≤ 4Nβ2^{−(ν+2)n}M(T) and μ_T{f = ρ*_ν} = μ_{∂T}{f = ρ*_ν} = 0. Push X_ν := T⌞{f ≥ ρ*_ν} by ψ and apply step 1; the shell estimates (Lip ψ ≤ c₂2^{i+4} on the i-th shell, whose μ_T-mass is ≤ Nβ2^{−(i+2)(n+1)}M(T)) make ψ_#X_ν and the homotopy terms mass-Cauchy, with limits Q₀, R₁, S₁: T − Q₀ = ∂R₁ + S₁, M(Q₀), M(R₁) ≤ cM(T), M(S₁), M(∂Q₀) ≤ cM(∂T). Q₀ = Φ_ψ(T) and Φ_h([[0,1]] × T) are IM by step 2 (finite Jacobian integrals by the shell estimates), so R₁ = 0 − Φ_h is IM by (IMC)(c). Q₀ is carried by the open n-faces F of the grid; on each, Q₀⌞F = u_F[[F]] with integer u_F and divergence variation V_F, ΣV_F ≤ M(∂Q₀). With integer medians β_F (step 3), P := Σβ_F[[F]] satisfies M(P) ≤ 2M(Q₀), M(Q₀ − P) ≤ c_nM(∂Q₀), M(∂P) ≤ cM(∂Q₀), P and ∂P are IM (integer face chains), and R := R₁, S := S₁ + (Q₀ − P) give T − P − S = ∂R with all supports within 2√P of spt T, resp. spt ∂T.
6. Scaling (Simon 5.3). Apply step 5 to δ_{ρ#}T, δ_ρ(x) := x/ρ (affinePushforward preserves IM and commutes with ∂), and push back: Q := Σβ_F[[ρF]] satisfies M(Q) ≤ cM(T), M(∂Q) ≤ cM(∂T), M(R) ≤ cρM(T), M(S) ≤ cρM(∂T), supports within 2√Pρ < 3√Pρ, and Q = 0 or M(Q) = ρⁿΣ|β_F| ≥ ρⁿ. This is (DTr), with c depending only on (P, m).

If z > 0, apply (DTr) with ρ := (2cz)^{1/(m+1)}: M(S) ≤ cρM(∂Z) = 0 gives S = 0, and M(Q) ≤ cz < 2cz = ρ^{m+1} gives Q = 0; so Z = ∂R and Y := R satisfies M(Y) ≤ cρz = c(2cz)^{1/(m+1)}z and spt Y ⊆ thickening(3√Pρ, spt Z). ∎

Source: parent V5 and T3. Uses (SL) = sibling slicing and (REP) of sibling foundations; (Isor) only for m := d − 1 (d ≥ 1, m + 1 = d < P).
